overview:
Not everyone wants to spend hours on the road or pack a suitcase every morning. This five-day itinerary keeps you in one riad in Marrakech and uses easy day trips to show you three other faces of Morocco: the green valleys of the High Atlas, the Atlantic port of Essaouira and the stony Agafay desert at sunset. In between, a licensed guide shows you the medina, and a cooking class teaches you to make the dishes you have been eating.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 5 days, 4 nights
• Base: one riad in the Marrakech medina – no hotel changes
• Type: private tour with your own driver; licensed city guide in Marrakech, mountain guide in Imlil
• Longest drive: Essaouira, about 2.5–3 hours each way; all other trips are 1–1.5 hours
• Activity level: easy; one gentle mountain walk of 2–3 hours
• Best months: March to May and September to November; possible all year

THE PLAN DAY BY DAY
• Day 1 – Marrakech with a licensed guide: Koutoubia, Bahia Palace, Ben Youssef madrasa, the souks and the Majorelle Garden.
• Day 2 – High Atlas: Imlil (65 km) and a walk to the Berber village of Aroumd below Jebel Toubkal.
• Day 3 – Essaouira (about 190 km): the port, the ramparts and the medina, with an argan cooperative on the way.
• Day 4 – Cooking class in the morning, then sunset, camels and dinner in the Agafay desert (about 40 km).
• Day 5 – Free morning for a hammam or the souks, then your airport transfer.

WHY THIS PLAN WORKS
One base means you unpack once and come home every evening to the same quiet courtyard. Each day trip is short enough to leave time for the city, and the order balances busy days with gentler ones: the medina first, while everything is new, the mountains and the ocean in the middle, and a relaxed cooking day before a sunset in the desert.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
First-time visitors, couples, families with children, travellers who prefer comfort to long drives, and anyone who wants mountains, ocean and desert in one short trip.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
The Agafay is a stony desert without big dunes. To sleep among the sand dunes of the Sahara, choose [the 6-day Morocco itinerary with the Sahara loop and Essaouira](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/morocco-itinerary-6-days-marrakech-the-sahara-loop-and-essaouira/fbca777d16e324c5ccb15043). If you would rather see the kasbahs of the south, swap a day for the [Ait Ben Haddou day trip](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/ait-ben-haddou-ouarzazate-day-trip-from-marrakech-over-the-atlas/7c3f043cd0b560a6f555e9c0).

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Book Majorelle Garden tickets online in advance, as timed slots often sell out. Bring comfortable shoes for the medina and the mountain walk, a warm layer for the Atlas and evenings in the Agafay, sun protection and a light scarf. Shoulders and knees covered is respectful in the medina and the villages. Carry some cash in dirhams for entrance fees, lunches and small purchases. Tell us your arrival time so we can arrange the airport pick-up.
descriptions:
What to expect: a full guided day in the medina of Marrakech, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, from its great monuments to the craft souks and a famous garden.

Your licensed guide meets you at your riad in the morning. You start at the Koutoubia mosque, whose 12th-century minaret is the landmark of the city, then walk through the lanes to the Bahia Palace, a 19th-century residence of courtyards, carved cedar ceilings and zellige tiles. Next comes the Ben Youssef madrasa, a former Koranic school with one of the most beautiful courtyards in Morocco.

At midday your guide leads you through the souks, where each lane once had its own trade: the dyers with skeins of coloured wool hanging overhead, the spice and herb sellers, the leather workers and the metal lantern makers. Your guide helps you find your way and explains how to bargain politely. After lunch your driver takes you to the Majorelle Garden in the new town: a cactus and bamboo garden around a cobalt-blue villa, created by the painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent.

In the evening, walk to Jemaa el-Fna square as the food stalls, musicians and storytellers fill it.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Koutoubia mosque and gardens.
09:45 – Bahia Palace.
11:00 – Ben Youssef madrasa.
12:00 – Dyers', spice and craft souks.
13:30 – Lunch (not included).
15:00 – Majorelle Garden.
16:30 – Return to your riad; free evening.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Majorelle tickets are sold by time slot; book them online as soon as your dates are fixed.
• Your guide never takes you to shops you do not want to visit; say what interests you.
• Wear comfortable shoes: the medina is best seen on foot.

INCLUDED: licensed city guide, driver for the Majorelle transfer, riad night with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, dinner, tips.

Overnight: Marrakech (riad)
Meals: breakfast

What to expect: a short drive into the High Atlas and a gentle guided walk of 2–3 hours through Berber villages and orchards, with lunch in a village house.

Your driver takes you south across the Haouz plain, past the village of Tahanaout and up the Mizane valley to Imlil (about 1,740 m), the main gateway to Toubkal National Park, about 1.5 hours from Marrakech. On clear days, the snow on the peaks is visible from the road in winter and spring.

In Imlil you meet a local mountain guide and set off on foot along mule paths through walnut, apple and cherry orchards and beside old irrigation channels to the village of Aroumd (about 1,900 m), built on a rocky spur facing the mountains. From above the village you look up the valley towards Jebel Toubkal (4,167 m), the highest peak in North Africa. Lunch is served in a family house or guesthouse, often on a terrace with a view, before you walk back down to Imlil and return to Marrakech in the late afternoon.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Departure from Marrakech.
10:00 – Arrival in Imlil, meet your mountain guide.
10:30 – Walk to Aroumd (about 1.5 hours up).
13:00 – Lunch in a village house (not included).
14:30 – Walk back down to Imlil.
16:00 – Drive back to Marrakech.
17:30 – Arrival at your riad.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Paths are rocky; wear trainers or walking shoes with a good grip.
• It is often 10 °C cooler than Marrakech: bring a warm layer.
• If you prefer not to walk, the guide can arrange a mule for part of the way.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, local mountain guide, riad night with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: Marrakech (riad)
Meals: breakfast

What to expect: a day by the Atlantic in Essaouira, a relaxed walled port town with a UNESCO-listed medina, about 2.5–3 hours from Marrakech.

You leave Marrakech in the morning and cross the plains towards the ocean. On the way, stop at a women's argan cooperative, where you see how the nuts are cracked by hand, roasted and pressed into oil, and look out for the goats that climb the argan trees in this region.

In Essaouira, the air is fresh and the pace is slower. Walk along the fishing port, where blue boats unload the catch and gulls circle overhead, then up onto the Skala de la Ville, the sea ramparts with their old bronze cannons and views over the waves. The whitewashed medina with its blue shutters is easy to explore on your own: woodcarvers' workshops in thuya wood, art galleries, spice shops and small cafés. For lunch, choose your fish at the grills by the port and have it cooked on the spot. You return to Marrakech in the early evening.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:00 – Departure from Marrakech.
10:00 – Argan cooperative (about 30 min).
11:00 – Arrival in Essaouira: port and ramparts.
13:00 – Lunch at the port fish grills (not included).
14:30 – Free time in the medina and on the beach.
17:00 – Departure for Marrakech.
19:30 – Arrival at your riad.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Essaouira is often windy and cooler than Marrakech: bring a light jacket.
• Agree the price of fish at the port grills before ordering.
• The goats in the trees are sometimes posed for photos by herders who ask for a tip.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, riad night with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: Marrakech (riad)
Meals: breakfast

What to expect: a hands-on Moroccan cooking class in the morning, then the Agafay desert at sunset with a camel ride and dinner under the stars.

In the morning your cook takes you to a local market to choose vegetables, herbs and spices, then teaches you to prepare a full Moroccan meal: salads, a tagine or couscous, and mint tea poured the traditional way. You eat what you have cooked for lunch and take the recipes home.

In the afternoon your driver takes you to the Agafay desert, about 40 km and 45 minutes south-west of Marrakech: a plateau of rolling, golden stony hills with the High Atlas on the horizon. As the light softens, a camel ride takes you across the hills to watch the sunset, followed by dinner at a desert camp – salads, tagine and fruit – with music around the fire and a sky full of stars, before you return to your riad.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:30 – Market visit and cooking class.
13:00 – Lunch of the dishes you cooked.
14:00 – Free time at your riad.
16:00 – Drive to the Agafay desert.
17:00 – Camel ride and sunset (time varies by season).
19:30 – Dinner at the camp.
21:30 – Return to Marrakech.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Tell us about any allergies or a vegetarian diet before the class.
• Evenings in the Agafay are cool, cold in winter: bring a warm layer.
• If you would like to spend the night in the desert, we can book a tent at the camp instead of returning.

INCLUDED: cooking class with market visit and lunch, transfer to the Agafay, camel ride, dinner, riad night with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks, quad biking (optional), tips.

Overnight: Marrakech (riad)
Meals: breakfast, lunch, dinner

What to expect: a free morning to enjoy Marrakech at your own pace, then your private transfer to the airport.

Enjoy a last breakfast in the riad courtyard. Depending on your flight time, try a traditional hammam with black soap scrub and massage, return to the souks for last purchases, or visit a place you missed – the Saadian Tombs, the Secret Garden or the Maison de la Photographie. Your driver collects you at the riad at the agreed time for the transfer to Marrakech-Menara airport, about 20–30 minutes away.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
Morning – Free time.
Afternoon – Transfer to the airport (time set by your flight).

GOOD TO KNOW
• Book a hammam a day ahead; your riad can recommend one.
• Change leftover dirhams before you fly: they cannot be exchanged outside Morocco.
• Leave at least 2.5 hours before an international flight.

INCLUDED: airport transfer.
NOT INCLUDED: activities, meals, tips.

Overnight: not included (end of the tour)
Meals: breakfast

faq.question: Do we change hotels?
faq.answer: No. You stay in the same riad in the Marrakech medina for all four nights and return there every evening, so you unpack only once.

faq.question: Is the Agafay the Sahara?
faq.answer: No. The Agafay is a stony desert of rolling golden hills about 40 km from Marrakech, with the Atlas on the horizon but no big sand dunes. It gives you the silence, sunsets and stars of the desert without long drives. For dunes, you need Merzouga or Zagora.

faq.question: Is it a private tour?
faq.answer: Yes. Your driver and guides work only with your group, and you can adjust start times, stops and the order of the days.

faq.question: How long are the drives?
faq.answer: Imlil is about 1.5 hours from Marrakech, the Agafay about 45 minutes and Essaouira about 2.5–3 hours each way. The Essaouira day is the only long drive.

faq.question: Is the mountain walk difficult?
faq.answer: No. The walk to Aroumd takes 2–3 hours in total on rocky mule paths, with about 200 m of ascent. Anyone in reasonable health can do it at a gentle pace, and a mule can carry you part of the way if needed.

faq.question: Which meals are included?
faq.answer: Breakfast every day at your riad, plus lunch on the cooking class day and dinner in the Agafay. Other lunches and dinners are not included, so you can choose restaurants in the medina, in Imlil or at the Essaouira fish grills.

faq.question: Are entrance fees included?
faq.answer: No. Tickets for the Bahia Palace, the Ben Youssef madrasa and the Majorelle Garden are paid separately. Majorelle tickets should be bought online in advance for a time slot.

faq.question: Is this itinerary good for families?
faq.answer: Yes. Short drives, one base, a gentle walk, the beach and port in Essaouira, a cooking class and a camel ride make it one of our most family-friendly trips. Tell us the children's ages if you need child seats.

faq.question: Can we stay a night in the Agafay?
faq.answer: Yes. Instead of returning to Marrakech after dinner on Day 4, you can sleep in a tent at the desert camp and wake up to the sunrise over the Atlas. Ask us when booking; it may change the price.

faq.question: Is airport pick-up included?
faq.answer: The transfer to the airport on Day 5 is included. We can also meet you at Marrakech-Menara airport on arrival; tell us your flight details.

faq.question: When is the best time for this itinerary?
faq.answer: Spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) are ideal. Summer is very hot in Marrakech but pleasant in Essaouira and the mountains. Winter is sunny by day, with snow on the Atlas peaks and cold evenings in the Agafay.

faq.question: Can we change the order or swap a day?
faq.answer: Yes. Because you stay in one riad, days can be swapped easily, for example to avoid wind in Essaouira or to replace a day with a trip to Ait Ben Haddou or the Ouzoud waterfalls.

faq.question: What should I pack?
faq.answer: Comfortable walking shoes, light clothing that covers shoulders and knees, a warm layer for the mountains and desert evenings, a light jacket for windy Essaouira, sunglasses, sun cream and a hat.
